# Groq Free GPT-OSS 20B screen — 26 September 2026

**Decision:** one newly frozen, scientific-first public-input call is justified as a screen of a distinct checkpoint. `openai/gpt-oss-20b` is not qualified for a default, and the failed `openai/gpt-oss-120b` trial is not evidence that it will pass. No 20B inference or production change has occurred.

[Groq's model page](https://console.groq.com/docs/model/openai/gpt-oss-20b) lists JSON Schema and Object modes, tool use, a 131,072-token context and a 65,536-token maximum output. The [current Free-plan limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits) list 30 RPM, 1,000 RPD, 8,000 TPM and 200,000 TPD for this exact model; exceeding a limit returns 429. Those are organization limits, so another user's usage or a per-project cap can reduce the available balance. The model page's per-token prices describe billable service, not a zero-price request guarantee after an account upgrade. [Groq's billing FAQ](https://console.groq.com/docs/billing-faqs) says Free-to-Developer upgrade needs a payment method and takes effect immediately. [Groq's data policy](https://console.groq.com/docs/your-data) makes inference ZDR available and excludes customer inputs/outputs from retained usage metadata.

The signed-in account readback on 26 September showed **Free — Current Plan, $0** and **Inference APIs ZDR — Enabled**. The organization's limit table listed `openai/gpt-oss-20b` at 30 RPM, 1,000 RPD, 8,000 TPM and 200,000 TPD; Default Project showed no custom lower limit. Global ZDR remains disabled, while the direct inference API is the intended boundary. The readback is current for a bounded screen, not a durable production billing control: the historical [120B candidate note](groq-free-alternative-2026-09-26.md) records that an operator-day attestation cannot detect a same-day plan upgrade. Recheck Free/ZDR immediately before any call, use only the dedicated campaign key and exact model, and stop on any mismatch. Do not use Groq's paid Developer service, built-in metered tools or model fallback.

The retained M1 near-complete local run reached 40/41 outer durable tasks but has **no provider-call or token totals** ([recovery receipt](../local-recovery196.json), [paused-run receipt](../local-run-paused197.json)); outer tasks cannot be substituted for requests. The historical 120B four-claim call consumed 2,273 tokens ([raw trial](groq-batch-2026-09-26-trial-1-live.json)), but that one-call figure cannot predict a full 20B run. At that illustrative size, 200,000 TPD would cover about 88 calls. The engine can request 24,000 output tokens on one research-overview call, while the Free plan allows only 8,000 combined tokens per minute; a documented model output ceiling does not prove that unchanged request shape works within this account quota. Whether Groq reserves the requested maximum against TPM is unverified. A full unattended run is therefore unqualified until measured end-to-end usage, rate-limit parking/recovery and report publication succeed without charges.

The cheapest remaining product screen is the existing fixed public four-claim batch through the real assessor under a **new** preregistration for 20B. Its first trial gets one physical request, no retry or fallback, exact served-model and usage evidence, and stops on a wrong completed label/quote, 429, missing evidence or provider error. The historical 120B protocol's `model_primary` requirement for an accepted contradiction is structurally unreachable after the local provenance guard; the new protocol must use the actual accepted contradiction method while retaining exact labels and self-contained evidence. Only a passing scientific gate warrants the separate tool, stream, long-input and reasoning checks, including the 24,000-token request shape. Advertised benchmarks are not claim-provenance or scientific-quality evidence.
